relationship.statement: A simple pendulum's swing period depends only on its length and gravity, not on its bob mass or small release angle. Increasing length slows the swing.
assumptions: Gravitational acceleration is fixed at g = 9.81 m/s^2 on Earth.
Air resistance and string mass are neglected.
Small-angle model: period stays independent of release angle.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the center of the test bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the test pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting release angle of the test pendulum from vertical.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Constant downward acceleration due to gravity (9.81 m/s^2).

quantities.label: Test period
quantities.meaning: Time for one complete back-and-forth swing of the test pendulum.

quantities.label: Ref period
quantities.meaning: Period of the fixed 1.0 m, 1.0 kg reference pendulum.

quantities.label: Test angle
quantities.meaning: Current angle of the test pendulum from vertical.

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the test bob at the bottom of its swing.

quantities.label: Gravity force
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational force acting on the test bob.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var refLen = 1.0; var refAngle0 = 20; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var a0 = inputs.angle0; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var refOmega = Math.sqrt(g / refLen); var period = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var refPeriod = 2 * Math.PI / refOmega; var angle = a0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var refAngle = refAngle0 * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var thetaRad = angle * Math.PI / 180; var refRad = refAngle * Math.PI / 180; var maxSpeed = omega * L * (a0 * Math.PI / 180); var weight = m * g; var bobX = 1.2 + L * Math.sin(thetaRad); var bobY = 2.7 - L * Math.cos(thetaRad); var bobSize = 0.15 + 0.8 * (m - 0.5) / 4.5; var arrowTipY = bobY - 0.14 * m; var refBobX = -1.4 + refLen * Math.sin(refRad); var refBobY = 2.7 - refLen * Math.cos(refRad); return { period: period, refPeriod: refPeriod, angle: angle, refAngle: refAngle, maxSpeed: maxSpeed, weight: weight, bobX: bobX, bobY: bobY, bobSize: bobSize, arrowTipY: arrowTipY, refBobX: refBobX, refBobY: refBobY, isSlower: L > 1.05, isFaster: L < 0.95, isMatched: Math.abs(L - 1.0) <= 0.05 }; }

lesson.title: What changes how a pendulum swings?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum with a fixed 1 m reference as both swing side by side. Change length, bob mass, and release angle to see what alters the period.
lesson.instructions: Adjust string length, bob mass, and release angle, then watch the swings and angle-time curves. Set length to 1.0 m while varying mass and angle to test what changes the period.
lesson.goal: String length controls a pendulum's period, while bob mass and small release angles leave the period unchanged.
